audit_type: Independent descriptive correctness and personalization audit; not a model experiment
scope: Five completed sample-trained item-neighbour runs on the frozen validation benchmark

inputs.executed_code: artifacts/experiments/cm-20261119-knn-conditional/source/experiments/campaign_neighbors.py and campaign_common.py, with that snapshot's src/cinematch evaluator
inputs.source_integrity: Every source_sha256 entry checked for each audited run. Same neighbour scoring implementation used across the audited sample configurations.

methods: Loaded checksum-verified original training and validation arrays; read only reserved user identities from the full-data manifest.
Confirmed no sample training user belongs to validation, legacy test or reserved fresh final holdout.
Checked saved movie-ID order and all-rating counts against original training arrays for every audited model.
Recomputed feedback counts directly from training arrays, using >=4 ratings for positive-feedback models and all ratings for observed-feedback models.
Checked every saved sparse row for top-K bound, unique neighbours and excluded self-neighbour.

Recomputed existing-model scores with snapshot scoring functions and supplied onboarding only; evaluated with the original metric implementation; matched every saved per-user metric row and top-five order.
Sampled 24 nonempty conditional rows using NumPy seed 23 and verified their first retained weights against direct intersections of training users who rated both titles >=4.
Identified popularity fallbacks by exact equality of the returned score vector with stored training counts; described existing nonfallback results without altering the algorithm.
Compared the existing signed variant's scores with zero to identify uninformative highest-score ties. No repair or alternative scoring variant was evaluated.

interpretation.correctness: No observed leakage, movie alignment error, sparse-row error or metric discrepancy explains these five recorded results.
interpretation.personalization: The conditional model's gain persists among users receiving nonfallback scores, with different rankings for different users. It combines co-like information with a strong preference for broadly liked titles; it is not simply the rating-count fallback.
interpretation.conditional_scope: The conditional model recommends popular titles: median recommended training support 4743 and no recommended slot below 100 training ratings. This is not evidence of long-tail discovery quality.
interpretation.positive_threshold_detail: Training positives are ratings >=4, while default positive inference weights are max(rating-3,0). Therefore 3.5-star seeds contribute; 177 of 500 validation users have at least one such seed.
interpretation.signed_failure_mode: For 16 users the signed scorer returns some negative values but no positive values. Untouched zero-score candidates win by catalogue-order tie breaking. Its fallback fires only when all scores are zero. Any repair requires a separately recorded experiment.

limitations: Validation results are exploratory after a multi-configuration search; bootstrap intervals do not correct for that selection.
The 498 ranking users exclude two users without recorded positive targets. Fallback counts include all 500 users; nonfallback ranking counts use only eligible users.
These are conditional descriptions of completed variants, not independent randomized evidence of causal mechanisms.
No new training seeds, training populations or alternative onboarding protocols were assessed by this audit.
Unobserved movie relevance remains unknown and retrospective exposure bias remains.
The fresh final holdout was not opened, and this audit makes no final-holdout performance claim.
